title: Premium Accounting Standard: Working Out What Must Reach the Plan to Settle a Supplement Premium Account
content:
This is the accounting basis on which the figure to settle a premium account under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies is worked out. The figure is the premium owed for the billing period now current, together with the charges standing on the account for the periods the settlement reaches back over and the policy fee falling due with it, less the money already standing to the policyholder's credit.

### 1. The months a billing period covers

The months a billing period covers are the months the policyholder's billing cadence bills at a time: twelve on an annual cadence, six on a semi-annual cadence, three on a quarterly cadence and one on a monthly cadence.

### 2. The monthly premium the policy is rated on

The monthly premium the policy is rated on is built from the plan letter's base monthly premium for a policyholder issued at 65. That base monthly premium is taken as it stands, whatever the policyholder's age.

That monthly premium is then multiplied by the plan letter's area factor, and by the plan letter's tobacco factor where the policy is rated as a tobacco user, before any discount is taken.

Where the plan holds the policy as taking the household discount, the plan letter's household discount is then taken from that monthly premium; where it does not, the monthly premium stands as rated.

No reduction is taken from that monthly premium.

### 3. The billing period now current

The premium owed for the billing period now current is then fixed. That period is valued at the amount posted for it.

### 4. The span reached back over

The settlement reaches back over the billing period now current alone. Every charge posted within the span reached back over is owed.

### 5. The policy fee

The policy fee is charged once a policy year and falls due with the settlement. The share of the annual policy fee falling on the months the billing period now current covers is added.

### 6. Money already received

Money already received is then set against what is owed. The payments that settled a billing period in full within the span reached back over are credited. Every return already credited on the account within the span reached back over is set against the settlement as well.

### 7. Putting the figures together

The premium for the billing period now current, the charges reached back over and the policy fee are added together, the credits and the returns are taken from that total, the figure is rounded to the cent once at the end, and where the credits and returns standing exceed what is owed nothing is payable and the difference stands to the policyholder's credit.

### Worked through on hypothetical figures

Take a policy on Ridgecrest Medicare Supplement Plan N, billed monthly, held as taking the household discount and not rated as a tobacco user, whose premium account carries one charge of 114.71 for the billing period now current and no payment or return at all.

The cadence is monthly, so the billing period covers 1 month. The base monthly premium at 65 for that plan letter is 118.60, taken as it stands. Multiplied by the area factor of 1.04 and rounded to the cent, that gives 123.34; no tobacco factor is applied. The household discount of 7 per cent taken from that leaves 114.71 when rounded to the cent. No reduction is taken for the way the policyholder pays.

The billing period now current is valued at the amount posted for it, being 114.71. The settlement reaches back over that period alone, and the charges posted within it come to 114.71. The share of the annual policy fee of 20.00 falling on the 1 month that period covers is 1.67 when rounded to the cent. Nothing has been credited and nothing returned.

Adding 114.71, 114.71 and 1.67 gives 231.09, and taking nothing from it leaves 231.09. Rounded to the cent once at the end, the figure to settle the account is 231.09.
